item.title: Peripheral Eye Scan Catch Alzheimer’s in Its Tracks
item.description: Researchers find that early Alzheimer’s markers appear in the peripheral retina, offering a new path for non-invasive early detection.

item.title: Study Shows Cognitive Recovery in Psychosis
item.description: It’s not a single path. A decade-long study reveals how the brain’s "growth chart" can predict recovery and treatment success in people with psychosis.

item.title: Astrocytes Discovered as Architects of Fear Memory
item.description: Star-shaped astrocytes have been unmasked as the master controllers behind how your brain learns—and unlearns—fear.

item.title: Teen Cannabis Use Doubles Psychosis and Bipolar Risk
item.description: One hit could have a two-year countdown. New research confirms that teen cannabis use doubles the risk of severe psychiatric disorders in young adulthood.

item.title: AI Rebirth: Turning Digital Footprints Into Living Legacies
item.description: A new study explores the rise of "AI resurrections," where generative AI reanimates the dead for entertainment, politics, and grieving.

item.title: Mapping the Brain’s Insulation: 10 Million Cells That Speed Up Your Thoughts
item.description: The brain's "wiring" just got a lot clearer. Scientists have mapped 10 million cells responsible for insulating your thoughts and protecting brain health.

item.title: Why Pain Lingers Longer in Women
item.description: It’s not in your head; it’s in your immune system. Scientists discover the biological "off-switch" that explains why chronic pain persists longer for women.

item.title: Toxic Exposure Can Trigger Disease for 20 Generations
item.description: Your health might be an echo from the past. A new study shows that toxic exposure 500 years ago could be the hidden root of chronic disease today.

item.title: Your DNA Might Be the Reason Music and Art Gives You Chills
item.description: A study of 15,500 people reveals that genetics account for 30% of why people experience "aesthetic chills" from music and art.

item.title: We All Speak Music: The Brain’s Constant Search for Harmony
item.description: Your brain is a secret musical expert. New research shows that even without formal training, we all use deep musical context to predict the next note.
